r.t: CANCELLATION & REFUND POLICY
This
Cancellation & Refund Policy
“Policy”

) sets out the rules that apply where a Booking is cancelled, a User does not attend an agreed handover, a Traveller refuses an Item, a journey or delivery cannot be completed, or a refund is requested.

This Policy forms part of Jibly’s Marketplace Terms and must be read together with them. Any capitalised term used in this Policy that is not separately defined here has the meaning given to it in the Marketplace Terms.

This Policy determines how Jibly will deal with the Booking and the related Payment, Traveller Compensation and Jibly Fee where a transaction does not proceed as originally agreed. The outcome may depend on the stage reached in the Booking, why it did not proceed, which party was responsible, what services had already been provided and the evidence reasonably available to Jibly.

Jibly may review the circumstances and determine, for Platform and payment purposes, whether an amount should be released, refunded, retained, reversed or placed on hold. Jibly’s decision under this Policy does not make Jibly a party to the carriage arrangement between the Sender and Traveller and does not determine any separate legal claim that one User may have against another.
Nothing in this Policy limits any statutory cancellation, refund or other consumer right that cannot lawfully be excluded.
BEFORE A BOOKING IS CONFIRMED
A Booking is not confirmed until the relevant Sender or Traveller has accepted the Booking request or Offer and the required payment process has completed successfully.

Before confirmation, either party may decide not to proceed. If the Sender’s payment method has only been authorised and the Booking is not confirmed, the authorisation will be released or allowed to expire through Stripe. No Traveller Compensation will be due and no cancellation charge will apply to an unconfirmed Booking.
CANCELLATION AFTER CONFIRMATION AND BEFORE HANDOVER
Once a Booking has been confirmed, the Payment will normally have been captured and the parties are expected to proceed with the Booking.

A User who can no longer proceed must notify Jibly and the other party as soon as reasonably possible. Simply failing to attend, ignoring messages or abandoning the Booking does not avoid the consequences of cancellation.

A cancellation after confirmation does not automatically entitle the Sender to a full refund. Jibly may consider who cancelled, why the cancellation occurred, how close the cancellation was to the agreed handover or Trip, whether the other party had already reasonably relied on the Booking, whether any genuine costs or inconvenience had been caused, and what marketplace services Jibly had already provided.

A User must not cancel a confirmed Booking merely because they have found another User, a cheaper arrangement or another way of completing substantially the same transaction and expect Jibly to refund fees already properly earned.
SENDER CANCELLATION, NO-SHOW OR FAILURE TO PROCEED

If the Sender cancels before handover, does not attend the agreed handover, fails to provide the Item, provides materially different Item details, or otherwise prevents the Booking from proceeding, Jibly may treat the Booking as a Sender-caused cancellation. Where the Platform provides a cancellation function, the Sender must use that function and select the reason that most accurately describes why the Booking is being cancelled.

Where the Traveller has not taken possession of the Item, some or all of the Traveller Compensation will normally be returned to the Sender. However, Jibly may take into account any genuine and reasonable loss or expense incurred by the Traveller in reliance on the confirmed Booking, particularly where the Sender cancelled at short notice or failed to attend without reasonable notice.

Jibly may retain all or part of the Jibly Fee where Jibly has already provided matching, Booking administration, payment processing or other marketplace services and retaining that amount is permitted by law.
TRAVELLER CANCELLATION, NO-SHOW OR FAILURE TO PROCEED

If the Traveller cancels after accepting a Booking, the Traveller must cancel through the Platform and provide the applicable reason. Where the cancellation is not caused by the Sender and occurs before handover, the Booking will normally be cancelled and the Sender will automatically receive a full refund of the Payment, including the Jibly Fee. The same position will normally apply where the Traveller does not travel, fails to attend the agreed handover or otherwise cannot carry the Item for a reason not caused by the Sender.

This does not apply where the Traveller was entitled to refuse the Item or stop the Booking because of the Sender’s breach, inaccurate description, prohibited or restricted Item, refusal to allow reasonable inspection, customs concern, safety concern or another matter for which the Sender was responsible.
Repeated Traveller cancellations or no-shows may result in restrictions, suspension or termination of the Traveller’s Account.
TRAVELLER REFUSAL AT HANDOVER

The Traveller may refuse an Item where it materially differs from the Item Request, cannot reasonably be inspected, appears unsafe or suspicious, exceeds an applicable limit, is prohibited or restricted, raises a customs or transport concern, or where the Sender has withheld or misstated important information.
Where the refusal is caused by the Sender’s breach or inaccurate information, the matter will be treated as a Sender-caused failure rather than a Traveller cancellation.

If the Item complies with the Booking and these Terms and the Traveller simply changes their mind or is unable to carry it for a reason unrelated to the Sender, the refusal will normally be treated as a Traveller cancellation.
The Traveller must report the refusal promptly and must not take possession of the Item if they have decided not to carry it.
MATERIAL CHANGES AND MUTUAL CANCELLATION

A User must not materially change a confirmed Booking without the other party’s agreement. This includes material changes to the Item, route, travel date, Recipient, handover arrangements or other important Booking details.
If one party proposes a material change and the other reasonably refuses it, Jibly may treat the resulting cancellation as caused by the party who proposed the change.

Where the Sender and Traveller genuinely agree that a Booking should be cancelled before handover, Jibly may cancel the Booking without attributing fault to either party. The Traveller Compensation will normally be returned where the Item has not been handed over. Treatment of the Jibly Fee will depend on the services already provided and applicable law.
TRAVEL DISRUPTION AND EVENTS OUTSIDE THE PARTIES’ CONTROL

A flight cancellation, serious delay, border restriction, transport disruption or similar event may prevent a Booking from proceeding even though neither User caused the problem. Where the Platform provides a specific travel-disruption reporting option, the affected User must use that option and provide the relevant information reasonably requested by Jibly.

Where this happens before handover, Jibly may allow the parties to rearrange the Booking or may cancel it and process an appropriate refund. The Traveller Compensation will normally be returned where the Traveller never took possession of the Item.
Jibly may consider the marketplace services already provided when deciding how the Jibly Fee should be treated, subject to applicable law.
AFTER HANDOVER, FAILED DELIVERY AND PARTIAL PERFORMANCE

Once the Traveller has physically accepted the Item, the Booking can no longer normally be cancelled as an ordinary pre-handover cancellation. Any later problem will instead be dealt with as a delivery, return, loss, damage, confiscation or Dispute under the Marketplace Terms.
A Sender cannot cancel after handover merely because they have changed their mind and require the Traveller to abandon the agreed Trip or immediately return the Item.

A failed first delivery attempt does not automatically entitle the Sender to a refund. If the Traveller attends the agreed delivery location but the Sender or Recipient is unavailable, provides incorrect information, refuses to accept the Item or otherwise prevents delivery, Jibly may treat the Traveller as having performed some or all of their obligations.

Where the Traveller has partly performed the Booking before completion becomes impossible, Jibly may take the extent of that performance into account when deciding how much Traveller Compensation should be released or refunded. The outcome does not have to be an all-or-nothing refund where that would not fairly reflect what occurred.

Where an Item must reasonably be returned, Jibly may require the parties to arrange its return. Reasonable return costs may be allocated to the party whose act, omission or breach caused the failed delivery. Where neither party was responsible, Jibly may determine how those costs should reasonably be dealt with.

Where the Traveller uploads delivery proof and delivery has not otherwise been confirmed, the Sender will have three days from submission of that proof to confirm delivery or raise a Dispute. If the Sender does neither within that period, and there is no other matter requiring review, the Booking may automatically close and the Traveller Compensation may be released.
LOST, DAMAGED, STOLEN OR CONFISCATED ITEMS
Loss, damage, theft, confiscation or non-delivery does not automatically result in a full refund.

Jibly may consider how the problem occurred, the conduct of the Sender and Traveller, the Item description, packaging, customs position, proof of handover and delivery, and any other relevant evidence.
Jibly does not provide insurance. A declared Item value does not create a guaranteed right to reimbursement or compensation.
Any refund, Payout adjustment or recovery relating to such an event will be dealt with under the Marketplace Terms and this Policy according to the circumstances and responsibility of the parties.
CANCELLATION BY JIBLY

Jibly may cancel, stop or place a Booking on hold where reasonably necessary because of suspected fraud, a Prohibited Item, safety concerns, payment problems, sanctions or compliance concerns, misuse of the Platform, breach of the Marketplace Terms, a legal requirement, or a restriction imposed by Stripe or another relevant provider.
Where Jibly cancels a Booking for reasons that were not caused by either User, amounts paid for services that cannot be provided will normally be refunded.

Where cancellation results from a User’s breach, fraud, prohibited conduct, inaccurate information or non-compliant Item, Jibly may take that conduct into account when deciding whether any amount should be refunded or retained.
REFUNDS AND THE JIBLY FEE
The Traveller Compensation and Jibly Fee are separate parts of the Payment and may be treated differently when a Booking is cancelled or fails.

The Jibly Fee relates to marketplace services that may already have been provided before cancellation, including matching, facilitating the Booking, payment administration and Platform access connected with the transaction.
Jibly may retain all or part of the Jibly Fee where this is reasonably justified by services already provided and permitted by law.
Refunds may therefore be full or partial depending on the circumstances. A failure to complete a Booking does not, by itself, mean that every part of the Payment must automatically be refunded.

Where Jibly approves a refund, it will normally be processed through Stripe to the original payment method. The time taken for the funds to appear in the Sender’s account may depend on Stripe, the card issuer, the bank and applicable banking times. Jibly is not responsible for currency conversion differences or third-party bank charges outside its control.
DISPUTES, EVIDENCE AND PAYMENT HOLDS

Where there is disagreement about a cancellation, no-show, refusal, failed delivery or refund, Jibly may place the Booking into an “Under Review” or similar status and hold the relevant Payment or Payout while the matter is reviewed.
Jibly may consider Platform messages, Booking information, Handover Codes, Delivery Codes, photographs, timestamps, payment records, travel information and any other reasonably relevant evidence.

Both parties must cooperate with the review and provide information reasonably requested by Jibly. A User must not fabricate, alter, hide or knowingly misrepresent evidence. Jibly may draw reasonable conclusions from a User’s failure to provide evidence that should reasonably be available to them.

Requests relating to a cancellation, no-show, refusal at handover or travel disruption must be raised without undue delay and normally within 7 days of the relevant event. This seven-day period does not extend the separate three-day period for contesting delivery proof before automatic completion and Payout. Jibly may consider a later request where there is a reasonable explanation for the delay or where applicable law requires it, but may decline to investigate a stale claim where the relevant facts can no longer reasonably be verified.

Once Jibly has completed a reasonable review and communicated its decision, that decision will normally be final for Platform and payment purposes unless there is a clear error, material new evidence or a legal reason requiring the matter to be reconsidered.
CHARGEBACKS, DUPLICATE RECOVERY AND OFF-PLATFORM CIRCUMVENTION
A Sender must not receive a refund from Jibly and then attempt to recover the same amount again through a chargeback or another payment dispute.
False, dishonest, duplicate or abusive chargebacks are prohibited.

Where a valid refund or chargeback arises after the Traveller has already received a Payout, Jibly may reverse or recover amounts properly due from the Traveller in accordance with the Marketplace Terms, Stripe’s processes and applicable law.

A User must not cancel a Booking and then complete substantially the same transaction outside Jibly in order to avoid the Jibly Fee or Platform rules. Where Jibly reasonably determines that a cancellation was used for off-platform circumvention, Jibly may refuse to refund the Jibly Fee, recover any properly due fee and take action against the relevant Account in accordance with the Marketplace Terms.
Repeated cancellations, no-shows, refund abuse, chargeback abuse or use of the cancellation process to manipulate the Platform may result in Account restrictions, suspension or termination.
JIBLY’S SERVICES

When you confirm a Booking, you are asking Jibly to begin providing its marketplace services immediately. Those services may include facilitating the match and Booking, processing the transaction, making Platform functionality available for the Booking, enabling communications between the parties, administering the Payment and providing the handover, delivery and dispute-management tools connected with the Booking.

By confirming a Booking, you expressly request that Jibly begins providing those services immediately, including where this is during any statutory cancellation period that may apply to Jibly’s services. You acknowledge that, if you exercise a statutory right to cancel after Jibly has started providing the services but before they have been fully performed, Jibly may be entitled to retain or charge a proportionate amount for the services already provided, to the extent permitted by law.

You also acknowledge that once Jibly has fully performed the marketplace services covered by the relevant contract, you may lose any statutory right to cancel those services where applicable law permits this. Confirming a Booking therefore constitutes your express request for immediate performance and your acknowledgement that any applicable statutory cancellation right may end once Jibly’s services have been fully performed.
This statutory cancellation right relates to Jibly’s marketplace services and is separate from your ability to cancel the underlying Booking between the Sender and Traveller.
HOW TO REQUEST A CANCELLATION OR REFUND
A cancellation, no-show, refusal or refund request must be submitted through the Platform where the relevant function is available, or by contacting Jibly at contact@jibly.io.
You must provide enough information for Jibly to identify the Booking, understand what happened and assess the request. Jibly may ask for supporting information or evidence before making a decision.
Submitting a refund request does not automatically entitle you to a refund or require Jibly to release or reverse funds before the circumstances have been reviewed.
CHANGES TO THIS POLICY

Jibly may update this Policy from time to time to reflect changes to the Platform, Booking or payment processes, cancellation and refund procedures, applicable law, regulatory requirements or Jibly’s business operations. The updated Policy will be made available on the Platform and will state when it takes effect. Where a change is material, Jibly may provide additional notice where reasonably appropriate. Unless required by law, an update will not retrospectively change the cancellation or refund rules applicable to a Booking confirmed before the updated Policy took effect.
CONTACT
If you have questions, please contact us at contact@jibly.io.
